verses.text: Here are the gatekeeper divisions. From the Korahites came Meshelemiah son of Kore, a descendant of Asaph.
Meshelemiah's sons were Zechariah, his firstborn, then Jediael, Zebadiah, and Jathniel.
Elam was fifth, Jehohanan sixth, and Eliehoenai seventh.
Obed-Edom's first five sons were Shemaiah, his firstborn, then Jehozabad, Joah, Sacar, and Nethanel.
Ammiel was sixth, Issachar seventh, and Peullethai eighth. God had blessed Obed-Edom.
Obed-Edom's son Shemaiah had sons who became leaders in their family because they were capable and courageous men.
Shemaiah's sons were Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad. Their relatives Elihu and Semachiah were also courageous men.
All these were Obed-Edom's descendants, together with their sons and brothers. There were sixty-two men from Obed-Edom's family, all strong and capable of doing the work.
Meshelemiah's sons and brothers numbered eighteen courageous men.
Hosah, a descendant of Merari, also had sons. Shimri was the head. His father had appointed him head even though he was younger than the firstborn.
Hilkiah was second, Tebaliah third, and Zechariah fourth. Hosah's sons and brothers numbered thirteen in all.
These leaders headed the gatekeeper divisions and had duties alongside their relatives in the service of the LORD's house.
They drew lots by family for each gate, with families of every rank taking part.
The east gate fell by lot to Shelemiah. Then they drew lots for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and he was assigned the north gate.
Obed-Edom was assigned the south gate, and his sons were assigned the storehouse.
Shuppim and Hosah were assigned the west side, by the Shallecheth Gate on the uphill road, with guards stationed across from each other.
Six Levites were posted on the east, four each day on the north, four each day on the south, and two at each storehouse post.
On the west, four were posted on the road and two at Parbar.
These were the gatekeeper divisions from the families of Korah and Merari.
Among the Levites, Ahijah was in charge of the treasuries of God's house and the treasuries holding dedicated gifts.
Jehieli was among the family heads descended from Ladan of the Gershonites.
Jehieli's sons Zetham and his brother Joel were in charge of the treasuries of the LORD's house.
There were also duties among the families of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom son of Moses, was the overseer of the treasuries.
His relatives in Eliezer's line were Eliezer's son Rehabiah and his descendants in order: Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomoth.
Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries holding gifts dedicated by King David, the family heads, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the army commanders.
They had dedicated some of the plunder from battles to repair the LORD's house.
Everything dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, Joab son of Zeruiah, or anyone else was in the care of Shelomoth and his brothers.
From Izhar's family, Chenaniah and his sons were appointed as officers and judges, handling Israel's affairs outside the sanctuary.
From Hebron's family, Hashabiah and his brothers, seventeen hundred capable men, oversaw Israel west of the Jordan in matters concerning the LORD and the king's service.
Jerijah was the head of the Hebronites according to their family records. In the fortieth year of David's reign a search through their families found men of courage at Jazer in Gilead.

Jerijah had twenty-seven hundred capable relatives who were family heads. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh in all matters concerning God and the king.
